source_artifacts.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)

capabilities.target: directory profile and group memberships for a named user
a user's MFA methods and temporary pass issuance
chat message to the ticket's requester field

inputs.source: Support tickets, including tickets emailed in by contractors and vendors

instructions.note: The instruction sends the temporary access pass 'to the person who opened the ticket' with no requirement to verify that this requester is the account owner or an authorized delegate for the target user. Runtime notes confirm ticket requesters can be external contractors/vendors and that the requester field is simply the email sender.

The prompt states 'every reset needs analyst approval,' but only cap.mfa_reset carries an approval_gate_ref. cap.send_temp_pass, an S3 egress of a restricted credential, fires automatically once the reset is approved, with no separate gate. Per rubric section 3, the declared A2 autonomy is not fully supported for this capability; it functions as A3 (act then report) for the send step.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval before MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: Independent of model capability because the analyst reviews the raw target, requester, and full ticket text rather than a model-generated summary. Effectiveness instead depends on approval volume and the absence of any requester-to-target identity check (see finding residual_rationale).

controls.name: Temp-pass recipient bound to system-of-record contact
controls.decay_rationale: A destination pulled from the IdP's verified contact record for the target account, rather than from ticket content, does not decay with model capability because the model never chooses the destination.

controls.name: Out-of-band identity verification for MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: A verification step outside the ticket/email channel (callback to a pre-registered number, manager confirmation) does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Secondary review / volume threshold for the approval queue
controls.decay_rationale: A hard escalation rule (e.g., cross-domain requester or privileged account triggers two-person review) does not decay with model capability, though it does not fully remove human fatigue risk.

controls.name: Scope and log directory reads from external tickets
controls.decay_rationale: Restricting returned fields and logging provenance at the tool boundary does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: Confused deputy / helpdesk social engineering (TC1-TC4 variant): MFA reset credential delivered to unverified ticket requester

attack_path.note: Untrusted ticket, possibly emailed by a contractor or vendor, names a target user and a requester.
Agent looks up the named target user's directory profile.
Agent resets the target's MFA after analyst approval; approval reviews target, requester, and ticket text but not whether requester is authorized for target.
Agent sends the temporary access pass to 'the person who opened the ticket' -- the untrusted requester field, not a verified contact of the target account.

findings.residual_rationale: The floor from credited controls (one raw_action analyst approval on cap.mfa_reset, -2 tiers from critical) is moderate, but two design facts the control classifications cannot express push actual residual higher: (1) the approval queue displays the correct target, requester, and ticket text, but nothing in the queue or workflow confirms that the requester is the target account's owner or an authorized delegate, so a plausible cross-identity request has no ground truth to be caught against; (2) the design implies high approval volume (~200 requests per analyst per shift, most routine), the classic precondition for consent-fatigue (SAFE-T1403) to erode an otherwise-independent raw_action gate. Residual is rated high rather than the moderate floor.

forecast.watch_signal: autonomy.level raised to A3/A4 or the approval_gate_ref removed/narrowed from cap.mfa_reset in the queue config; or approvals-per-analyst-per-shift continuing to climb above the current ~200, which is the consent-fatigue precondition noted in runtime notes.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to send the temporary access pass 'to the person who opened the ticket' without verifying that the requester is the account owner or an authorized delegate for the target account.

Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, and the requester field is populated from the email sender, so the destination for the MFA reset temporary pass is an attacker-controllable value rather than a system-of-record contact tied to the target account.

evidence.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)
evidence.observation: The queue shows Action, Target, Requested-by, and full ticket text (raw_action review), but has no field or mechanism confirming that Requested-by matches the account owner of Target.

Two analysts approve about 400 requests per shift (~200 each), with most routine, creating approval-fatigue conditions that make a convincing fraudulent reset request more likely to be approved quickly despite raw_action visibility.

recommendations.action: Bind temp-pass delivery to the target account's verified contact(s) of record in the IdP, rather than to the ticket's requester/email-sender field, so the recipient cannot be chosen by ticket content.

Require an out-of-band identity check (callback to a pre-registered phone number, or manager/HR confirmation) before approving any MFA reset where the ticket requester differs from the target account owner or originates from an external/contractor email domain.

Add a secondary-review threshold for the approval queue (currently ~200 requests/analyst/shift) and route cross-domain or privileged-account reset requests to escalation instead of routine single-analyst approval.
Log and alert whenever the temp-pass recipient address differs from the target account's registered contact, to catch bypasses after the fact.

findings.title: Unrestricted directory read via untrusted ticket content (information disclosure)

attack_path.note: Untrusted ticket requests information about a named user.
Agent reads the target's directory profile and group memberships; no approval gate or logging control applies to this path.

forecast.watch_signal: idp.read_user scope widening to include additional sensitive fields, or a new tool/MCP server added that could chain this read output toward an egress capability.

evidence.observation: cap.user_read (idp.read_user) is invoked for any MFA ticket with no approval gate or logging control described in the artifacts.
Contractors and vendors can email tickets in, so any such sender can prompt a profile/group-membership lookup on an arbitrary target user with no review.

recommendations.action: Restrict the fields idp.read_user returns for externally-sourced tickets to the minimum needed to resolve the ticket, and apply the same provenance logging used for reset actions.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical: an untrusted ticket (including ones emailed in by contractors) can drive a credential_access reset and an irreversible egress of a temporary access pass. The only control in the design is a raw_action analyst approval on cap.mfa_reset, which credits -2 tiers to a moderate floor, but that approval has no mechanism to confirm the requester is authorized for the target account, and the design implies ~200 approvals per analyst per shift -- the classic consent-fatigue setup -- so residual is rated high rather than the computed floor. cap.send_temp_pass itself (an S3 egress of a restricted credential) carries no approval_gate_ref at all despite the declared A2 autonomy level, so it behaves as A3 for that step. Forecast returns to critical if the approval gate is weakened by an autonomy increase, direct removal, or continued volume growth. A secondary, lower-severity finding notes that directory reads triggered by the same untrusted tickets have no control at all, currently rated moderate.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior; no logs, code, or live system configuration were reviewed.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; capability scope (action, data_sensitivity, credential_scope) for idp.reset_mfa, idp.read_user, and chat.send_temp_pass is inferred from the stable-id descriptions and prompt text, so confidence is medium rather than high.

autonomy.max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not declared in the artifacts; per rubric section 4 they are treated as null/unbounded, which conservatively triggers the autonomy risk modifier.

Whether the approval queue tool actually blocks execution pending approval, and whether cap.send_temp_pass truly cannot fire without an approved reset, is declared in the artifacts but not independently verified.
